**Authentication for go2rtc's ONVIF server.** With `api: username/password` set, the ONVIF server now asks ONVIF clients
for that same username and password, in the way ONVIF clients send them. Home Assistant's ONVIF integration on another machine
can now use PTZ through go2rtc, and the `user`/`password` in Frigate's `onvif:` settings are the real login.

Builds on [v1.9.15-baichuan.2](https://github.com/privatecoder/go2rtc/releases/tag/v1.9.15-baichuan.2) (PTZ for `bc://`
cameras) and [v1.9.15-baichuan.1](https://github.com/privatecoder/go2rtc/releases/tag/v1.9.15-baichuan.1) (the native Baichuan
source).

## Highlights

- **The same credentials as the API**: a request is accepted with a WS-Security `UsernameToken` in the SOAP header
  (`PasswordDigest` or `PasswordText`, what Frigate and Home Assistant send) or with HTTP Basic auth. No new config options.
- **Requests from `127.0.0.1` need no credentials**, unless `local_auth: true` is set, the same rule as for the API. Frigate's
  bundled go2rtc keeps working unchanged.
- **Refused requests** get HTTP 400 with the ONVIF fault `ter:NotAuthorized` ("Sender not authorized"), which ONVIF clients
  report as a login error.
- **Calls clients make before logging in** (`GetSystemDateAndTime`, `GetCapabilities`, `GetServices`,
  `GetServiceCapabilities`, `GetHostname`) are answered without credentials, as the ONVIF specification asks. They no longer make
  go2rtc log in to the cameras unless the request is authorized. Everything else, and all of PTZ, needs credentials.
- **Every other path on port 1984 keeps the API's HTTP Basic check.** The ONVIF exemption follows the handler that serves the
  request, not the request path, so encoded or unusual paths cannot reach the web UI or the API without a login.
- **Credentials stay out of the logs**: the SOAP header is removed from request dumps at debug and trace level.
- **Without an API username nothing changes**: responses are byte-identical to the previous release.

## Usage

```yaml
# Frigate config.yml
go2rtc:
  api:
    username: someuser       # optional: switches authentication on
    password: somepass
cameras:
  e1-zoom:
    onvif:
      host: 127.0.0.1         # go2rtc, here inside the Frigate container
      port: 1984
      profile: e1-zoom        # the go2rtc stream name
      user: someuser          # always set these
      password: somepass
```

**Always set `user` and `password` in Frigate's `onvif:` block.** Frigate's ONVIF library fails with "bad argument type:
NoneType(None)" when no `user` is set. Without an API username any value works; with one, they must be the API username and
password (from `127.0.0.1` they are not checked unless `local_auth: true`).

Details: [internal/onvif/README.md](https://github.com/privatecoder/go2rtc/blob/v1.9.15-baichuan.3/internal/onvif/README.md#authentication).

## Tested

- Frigate's ONVIF client (onvif-zeep-async 4.3.0) from another machine: correct credentials get the profiles and send PTZ
  commands, a wrong password or user gets "Sender not authorized".
- Request shapes of other ONVIF clients (SOAP 1.1 and 1.2, WS-Addressing headers, `mustUnderstand`, `wsu:Timestamp`, XML
  declaration and BOM, several timestamp formats) are accepted with correct credentials.
- Probes for bypasses: encoded and unclean paths, `base_path` below `/onvif/`, all HTTP methods; tokens outside the SOAP header,
  in comments, CDATA or a second document; credentials in logs. All refused or clean.
- Unit tests with the race detector, and a byte comparison against the previous release without credentials.

## Known limitations

- A nonce is not remembered, so a captured request can be replayed for up to 5 minutes. On an untrusted network, use HTTPS
  (`api: tls_listen`).
- The camera credentials are still those of the `bc://` URL; the ONVIF login only controls who may use go2rtc's ONVIF server.

## Downloads

Binaries are built by GitHub Actions from this tag for Linux amd64, Linux arm64 and macOS arm64. The Linux files are plain
executables; the macOS one is zipped. `SHA256SUMS.txt` lists the checksums.

**Frigate**: save `go2rtc_linux_amd64` (or `_arm64`) as `/config/go2rtc`, make it executable (`chmod 755`) and restart Frigate.

Docker image (linux/amd64, linux/arm64): `ghcr.io/privatecoder/go2rtc:1.9.15-baichuan.3` or `ghcr.io/privatecoder/go2rtc:latest`.
